text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- President Martti Ahtisaari opening parliament's spring session wishes that the current government would stay in office its full term to spring 1999.
- Police investigating tax fraud in connection with imports of some 50 Harley Davidson motorcycles.
- Finland's communist party SKP returns to the official party register after an 18-month absence, aiming to get 9,000 members. @
- Finland's large cities' budget surpluses to fall 3.5 billion markka this year to 0.9 billion markka, researcher says.
- Man in Turku fined for tormenting a turtle.
- Finland wants the European Union to bloc cheap imports of potato chips from Belgium and the Netherlands to Finland. Officials say it looks like dumping and harms Finnish producers.
- Metsa-Serla's and UPM-Kymmene's Metsa Rauma pulp mill has brought only 1,500 permanent jobs, study shows.
- Finland beat Russia 5-1 in four-country ice-hockey tournament in Stockholm. @
AAMULEHTI
- Finnish airforce officers suspect that foreign reconnaissance flights over the Baltic Sea can listen to conversations on digital GSM mobile phones.
- Some 600 mobile phones a year are stolen in the southwestern city of Tampere alone, police says.
- Delivery of sixteen rail buses ordered by the state railways has been delayed by a year as Spanish GEC Alsthom gave priority to wagons ordered by London underground. @
DEMARI
- President Martti Ahtisaari in his opening speech in parliament called on the tax administration to correct unfair taxation that has hit some businesses.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Thousands of planned houses will not be built if the state removes its interest subsidies in 1998, says director of union cooperative VVO group, Ben Grass.
- Steel imports from Russia move freely this year as expiry of EU-Russian agreement at the turn of the year abolished the need for import quotas, officials say. @
-- Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 242
